# Command reference

Every command prints exactly one JSON object (the envelope) on stdout. See [CLI and envelope](./cli.md) for the output contract and exit codes.

Global option: `-C, --root <dir>` runs the command against another repository (default: the nearest ancestor with `.git`).

## version

### `metator version`

Print the MetatorAI version

```bash
metator version [options]
```

## help

### `metator help`

List available commands

```bash
metator help [options]
```

## changed

### `metator changed`

Files changed against a git ref (committed on the branch, staged, unstaged, untracked)

```bash
metator changed [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--base <ref>` | git ref to compare against | `"HEAD"` |

## arch

### `metator arch init`

Propose metator/architecture.yml from the packages, Nx and Turborepo boundaries; never overwrites

```bash
metator arch init [options]
```

### `metator arch analyze`

Analyze the package graph; writes .metator/arch/report.json and report.md

```bash
metator arch analyze [options]
```

### `metator arch check`

Fail on violations the change adds: not at the base, not in the baseline, not excepted

```bash
metator arch check [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--base <ref>` | compare against the merge base with this ref |  |
| `--strict` | new warnings fail too |  |
| `--sarif <file>` | also write the new violations as SARIF 2.1.0 (code scanning) |  |

### `metator arch baseline`

Accept the current violations in metator/arch-baseline.json (--tighten only drops fixed ones)

```bash
metator arch baseline [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--tighten` | keep only baseline entries that still occur; never accept new ones |  |

### `metator arch cycles`

Cycles between packages, with the imports that close them

```bash
metator arch cycles [options]
```

### `metator arch declared`

Dependencies imported but not declared, declared but not imported, and version drift

```bash
metator arch declared [options]
```

### `metator arch schema`

Print the JSON Schema of metator/architecture.yml

```bash
metator arch schema [options]
```

Shards per package with card and rules; lenses run per shard

## eval

### `metator eval run`

Run the headless review for every golden case (and repeat), then score the outputs

```bash
metator eval run [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--command <template>` | e.g. 'scripts/review-case.sh {case} {base} {head} {out}' **Required.** |  |
| `--runs-dir <dir>` | where each run writes &lt;case&gt;/&lt;run&gt;/ | `".metator/evals"` |
| `--repeat <n>` | runs per case (stability) | `3` |
| `--timeout-ms <ms>` | per run | `1800000` |

### `metator eval score`

Precision, recall, blocking precision, false blocks and decision variance from run outputs

```bash
metator eval score [options] <runs-dir>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<runs-dir>` | directory with &lt;case&gt;/&lt;run&gt;/findings/merged.json and verdict.json | |

### `metator eval compare`

Fail when the scores got worse (gate for changes to agents, skills and instructions)

```bash
metator eval compare [options] <before> <after>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<before>` | EvalReport of the base | |
| `<after>` | EvalReport of the change | |
| `--tolerance <ratio>` | allowed drop per number | `0.02` |

### `metator eval schema`

Print the JSON Schema of a golden eval case

```bash
metator eval schema [options]
```

### `metator run checkpoint`

Write the run's state summary to log.md (before a context compaction)

```bash
metator run checkpoint [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |

### `metator run handoff`

Write handoff.md from the run directory: stage, approvals, artifacts, recent log, how to resume

```bash
metator run handoff [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |
| `--log-lines <n>` | recent log entries to include | `10` |

### `metator run close`

Write summary.json (final telemetry) for a finished run; --aborted --reason aborts an active one

```bash
metator run close [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |
| `--aborted` | abort an active run first (needs --reason) |  |
| `--reason <text>` | why the run is aborted |  |

### `metator run status`

Show the current stage, what it expects and recent history

```bash
metator run status [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |

### `metator run schema`

Print the JSON Schema of a run artifact written by a worker

```bash
metator run schema [options] <artifact>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<artifact>` | artifact (one of: analysis, research, summary) | |

### `metator run list`

List runs, newest first

```bash
metator run list [options]
```

### `metator run continue`

Continue a run: pick one that waits for you or stopped, drive it again and watch it

```bash
metator run continue [options] [run]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | run id (default: pick in a terminal, else the latest active run) | |
| `--host <host>` | AI host (default: the one the run used) (one of: claude, copilot, scenario) |  |

### `metator run drive`

Carry the run stage by stage: scripts, agents through an AI host, questions to people

```bash
metator run drive [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |
| `--host <host>` | AI host for the agents (default: first of hosts.targets) (one of: claude, copilot, scenario) |  |
| `--detach` | keep driving in the background after this command returns |  |
| `--max-steps <n>` | stop after this many stage transitions | `200` |

### `metator run stop`

Stop the process driving the run; the run stays where it is and can continue

```bash
metator run stop [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |

### `metator run questions`

Questions waiting for a person: HITL gates, agents asking, tool permissions

```bash
metator run questions [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | only this run (default: every run) |  |
| `--all` | include answered questions |  |

### `metator run answer`

Answer a question; the drive waiting for it continues

```bash
metator run answer [options] <question>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<question>` | question id, e.g. q001 | |
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |
| `--choice <labels...>` | the option label(s) chosen |  |
| `--text <text>` | your own words (with Other, or a reason with Reject) |  |
| `--by <name>` | who answers **Required.** |  |

### `metator run activity`

What the drive did: stages, agents, tools, questions, answers, transitions

```bash
metator run activity [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | run id (default: latest) |  |
| `--tail <n>` | only the last n entries |  |

## worktree

### `metator worktree new`

Create .metator/wt/&lt;id&gt; on branch metator/&lt;id&gt; with a free block of ports

```bash
metator worktree new [options] <id>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<id>` | worktree id (lowercase letters, digits, -) | |
| `--base <ref>` | ref to branch from | `"HEAD"` |
| `--run <id>` | the run that works in it |  |
| `--ports <count>` | how many ports to lease | `20` |

### `metator worktree list`

Worktrees with their branch, ports, run status and whether they hold uncommitted work

```bash
metator worktree list [options]
```

### `metator worktree rm`

Remove a worktree and free its ports; uncommitted work needs --force

```bash
metator worktree rm [options] <id>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<id>` | worktree id | |
| `--force` | remove even with uncommitted changes (they are lost) |  |

### `metator worktree prune`

Remove worktrees of finished runs older than N days; never one with uncommitted work

```bash
metator worktree prune [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--older-than <days>` | minimum age in days | `7` |
| `--dry-run` | report only |  |

## env

### `metator env discover`

How this repository starts (compose files, start scripts, Procfile, Makefile), with evidence

```bash
metator env discover [options]
```

### `metator env init`

Write the discovered environment to metator/environment.yml (never overwrites)

```bash
metator env init [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the proposal without writing it |  |

### `metator env up`

Start services in order of what they need, and wait until each is ready

```bash
metator env up [options] [services...]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[services]` | services to start (default: every service that is not on-demand) | |
| `--profile <name>` | start the services of a profile |  |
| `--worktree <id>` | start in this worktree, on its ports (default: this checkout) |  |
| `--affected` | start only the services the changes touch (their `paths`), and what they need |  |
| `--base <ref>` | with --affected: compare against this ref (default: where the worktree branched off) |  |

### `metator env analyze`

Measure a cold and a warm start in throwaway worktrees and recommend how to start faster

```bash
metator env analyze [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--cold` | restart running shared services first, so their start is measured too |  |

### `metator env pool`

Worktrees with their services already up; `run init --worktree` takes a free one

```bash
metator env pool [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--size <n>` | keep this many free worktrees started |  |
| `--drain` | stop and remove the free ones |  |

### `metator env down`

Stop the services of this checkout or a worktree (shared ones only with --shared)

```bash
metator env down [options] [services...]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[services]` | services to stop (default: all) | |
| `--worktree <id>` | stop in this worktree |  |
| `--shared` | also stop shared services, which other worktrees may use |  |

### `metator env status`

Each service: where it runs, whether it is up, its ports

```bash
metator env status [options]
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--worktree <id>` | the services of this worktree |  |

### `metator env logs`

The last lines a started service wrote

```bash
metator env logs [options] <service>
```

| Argument or option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `<service>` | service id | |
| `--worktree <id>` | the service of this worktree |  |
| `--lines <n>` | how many lines | `50` |

### `metator env schema`

Print the JSON Schema of metator/environment.yml

```bash
metator env schema [options]
```
